title: The affordance surface offers deployment.deploy per goal on deploy:goalId, withheld when no target is bound
description:
PRODUCER ROW filed by architect-b63fabf3 on 2026-09-06 at governor-afbde490's 13:50Z direction (item 1 of five). Consumer is task-84cd2e55aae942cf8d56657308215fde, which declares dependsOn against this row.

THE GAP IS AN IDENTITY MISMATCH, NOT AN ABSENCE - and that distinction is why a literal grep missed it. worker-f72a1438 corrected an earlier report of "zero deployment offers": `affordance-read.ts:234` iterates `BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS` generically and `:282-284` CAN emit a ready, uncommitted deployment kind. The offer exists; it is aimed at the wrong aggregate.

MEASURED BY ME AT HEAD:
- `bootstrap-sequence.ts` `aggregateIdFor` falls through to `default: return subject ?? request.projectId` for the deployment kinds - so a generic deployment offer targets the PROJECT.
- `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-deployments.tsx:80-86` finds its offer with `row["commandKind"] === "deployment.deploy" && row["targetAggregateId"] === `deploy:${goalId}``.
A project-targeted offer therefore never matches the card, and the card renders nothing while the surface believes it offered something.

THE SEMANTIC QUESTION THIS ROW MUST SETTLE, and it is the reason the row is not a one-line change. The durable target is keyed PER (project, environment) - `deployTargetAggregateId` = `deploy-target:<projectId>:<environment>` (deploy-target-contracts.ts:84). The card keys its offer PER GOAL. Those are different granularities, and the row must decide and DOCUMENT which authority the offer carries: a goal-scoped offer whose environment is chosen at dispatch, or one offer per (goal, environment). Do not guess in the browser - whatever is decided, the surface states it and the card reads it.

WITHHELD WHEN NO TARGET IS BOUND. The consumer's DoD 3 requires the card to be ABSENT rather than a dead button when the daemon offers no deploy. That distinction is produced HERE: with a bound target the offer appears, without one it does not. That is what makes "absent" mean something an operator can trust, and it is now measurable because task-79f8c7c0 composes the real target reader.

NOT IN SCOPE: the deployment-state read, the target-binding control, the browser mount, the e2e seam, and any change to how `deployment.deploy` executes.

VERIFICATION COMMAND for moe.complete_task: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. Also `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file.
definitionOfDone: The affordance read offers `deployment.deploy` targeted at `deploy:<goalId>` for a goal whose environment has a BOUND target, asserted BY VALUE on `targetAggregateId` - the card matches that exact string (goal-deployments.tsx:80-86), so an id that merely looks right is an offer nothing can render. Assert against the production surface read, not a hand-built frame.

The offer is WITHHELD when no target is bound for that environment. Assert the offered-kind SET so 'offers nothing for deploy' and 'offers something else' are one assertion - the consumer's card must be ABSENT rather than dead, and that distinction is produced here.

THE GRANULARITY DECISION IS MADE AND WRITTEN DOWN in a comment on the offer site: the durable target is per (project, environment) while the offer is per goal, so state which authority the offer carries and how the environment is determined at dispatch. A test asserts the decided shape. Do not leave the browser to infer it.

The generic project-targeted deployment offer no longer reaches the card's matcher by accident: assert that whatever the surface emits for deployment kinds, the card's exact matcher finds the goal-scoped offer and does NOT find a stale project-scoped one. Name in the completion record whether the generic path still emits a project-targeted offer and, if so, why it is harmless.

Every existing asserting consumer of the affordance surface is checked and named. `affordance-read.test.ts` and `affordance-read-planning.test.ts` both assert offered sets; say which needed an arm and why the other did not. A whole-tree census is required, not a package-scoped one: `tests/integration/**` and `tests/e2e/**` assert against this surface and are invisible to a grep under apps/daemon.

MUTATION DRILL, quoted with its failing line: target the offer at the project aggregate instead of `deploy:<goalId>` and confirm the DoD-1 arm goes RED - that reproduces exactly the defect this row exists to fix. Restore per global rail 13: back the path up out of tree, restore from the backup rather than `git checkout --`, prove by sha256 in a separate call.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file.
taskRails: THE OFFER'S TARGET IS `deploy:<goalId>`, ASSERTED BY VALUE. The card, the claim ledger and the board all fence on the exact work-item key; a near-miss renders nothing and looks like a UI bug for the rest of its life.
WITHHELD MEANS ABSENT, NOT DISABLED. The consumer's card is absent when no deploy is offered; producing a deploy offer with no bound target would put a dead button in front of an operator.

STATE THE GRANULARITY, DO NOT LEAVE IT TO THE BROWSER. Target is per (project, environment); the offer is per goal. Whatever is decided, the surface states it and the card reads it - a browser that infers the environment is inventing authority.

CENSUS THE WHOLE TREE FOR ASSERTING CONSUMERS, not just apps/daemon. `tests/integration/**` and `tests/e2e/**` assert on offered sets and are invisible to a package-scoped grep - that exact miss cost task-217f40b7 three extra consumers found in final review.
DO NOT CHANGE HOW `deployment.deploy` EXECUTES. This row decides what is OFFERED; the engine, its refusal order and its receipt belong to their own rows.

FINDING 1 — THE GOAL ID IS NOT IN `aggregateIdFor`'s SCOPE, so step 2's edit site moves. Step 2 says add the deployment case to `aggregateIdFor`. The goal reaches the affordance surface as `PlanningSubject` instead, and `bootstrapAggregateId` (affordance-read.ts:143-155) already handles exactly this — it returns `publish:${planningSubject.goalId}` for `repository.publish` BEFORE delegating to `aggregateIdFor`. So the affordance-side change belongs in `bootstrapAggregateId`, mirroring that line, which is the same precedent step 2 names. This is the "if a goal is genuinely not in scope, say so" branch the step anticipated, and I am taking it.

FINDING 2 — WITHHOLDING CANNOT BE A BARE OFFER SKIP; IT MUST GO THROUGH `surfaceMissing`. affordance-read.test.ts:563 asserts SET EQUALITY between the emitted offers and the READY steps: `expect(offered).toEqual(expected)`, where `expected` is every READY bootstrap step (plus COMMITTED policy.install). A `deployment.deploy` step left READY with its offer skipped breaks that invariant and reds an existing arm — which is a truer test than mine and must not be weakened. The existing seam for precisely this is `surfaceMissing` (:209-213), which already appends a SYNTHETIC missing prerequisite (`policy.install` for `project.activate`) beyond the durable ledger's own. Unbound target therefore becomes a missing prerequisite: the step returns BLOCKED at :272-278 before any offer is pushed, the set-equality invariant holds untouched, and the absence is NAMED in `missing` rather than silent. That is strictly better for DoD 2 as well — the consumer's card is absent AND the surface says why.

FINDING 3 — "BOUND" NEEDS AN ENVIRONMENT ROSTER, and there is a closed one. `DeployTargetPort = (environment) => DeployTarget | null` (deploy-ports.ts:41) cannot be asked "is anything bound" without a name. `ENVIRONMENT_NAMES = ["preview", "production", "verify"]` (environment-contracts.ts:29) is the closed roster, so bound means `ENVIRONMENT_NAMES.some((env) => target(env) !== null)`. implementationPlan.description:
TARGET THE OFFER AT THE GOAL (DoD 1). Give the deployment kinds a real aggregate id instead of the project fallthrough.

In `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts` `aggregateIdFor`, add the deployment case returning `deploy:<goalId>` - the EXACT string the card matches (goal-deployments.tsx:80-86). Follow the shape of the existing `repository.publish` case (:163), which already derives a goal-scoped key rather than falling through.

ASSERT BY VALUE, NEVER BY SHAPE (rail 1). The card, the claim ledger and the board all fence on the exact work-item key; an id that merely looks right renders nothing and reads as a UI bug for the row that consumes it. Build the string from the goal id with no separator drift - `deploy:` then the id, nothing else.

WHERE DOES THE GOAL ID COME FROM? The generic loop at affordance-read.ts:234 iterates kinds, not goals. Determine how the planning subject / goal is in scope at that call site (the `planningSubject` parameter at :231 is the likely source, and `bootstrapAggregateId("plan.propose", config.projectId, planningSubject)` at :233 shows it being used for exactly this purpose). If a goal is genuinely not in scope for the generic loop, that is a finding: say so and emit the deployment offer from the per-goal path instead, rather than inventing an id.

DO NOT CHANGE HOW `deployment.deploy` EXECUTES (rail 5) - this row decides what is OFFERED. The engine, its refusal order and its receipt are other rows'.
implementationPlan.note:
THE OFFER IS NOW GOAL-SCOPED (DoD 1), and the edit site moved for the reason step 1 recorded — the step anticipated this branch and I took it.

WHERE, AND WHY NOT `aggregateIdFor`. The step named `bootstrap-sequence.ts` `aggregateIdFor`. That function cannot produce `deploy:<goalId>` on an affordance read: its own `repository.publish` case (:163-167) reads goalId from the request PAYLOAD, and an affordance read carries no request payload — `bootstrapAggregateId` calls it with a synthesised `{ kind, projectId }` and a `DEFAULT_SUBJECTS` lookup that has no deployment entry, which is exactly why the fallthrough returned `request.projectId`. The goal reaches this surface as `PlanningSubject` instead, and `bootstrapAggregateId` (affordance-read.ts:143) already resolves goal-scoped kinds from it BEFORE delegating — `repository.publish` -> `publish:${planningSubject.goalId}` is the precedent the step told me to follow, and it lives there, not in the table. So one line beside it:

  if (kind === "deployment.deploy") return `deploy:${planningSubject.goalId}`;

BY VALUE, NOT BY SHAPE (rail 1). The template is `deploy:` + the goal id and nothing else — no trailing separator, no project prefix, no encoding — copied against the card's own literal at goal-deployments.tsx:83-85 (`row["targetAggregateId"] === `deploy:${goalId}``). Byte-for-byte comparison in the step-4 arm rather than a regex.

DoD 3's COMMENT IS WRITTEN AT THE OFFER-IDENTITY SITE, as reasoning rather than restatement: one offer PER GOAL; the environment is chosen at DISPATCH and travels in the payload (`daemon-command-payload-keys.ts` declares `deployment.deploy` as ["environment", "sha"], so a per-environment offer would put the environment in two places that can disagree); the durable target is keyed per (project, environment) via `deployTargetAggregateId`, a DIFFERENT axis that deliberately does not appear in the offer identity; the card reads the target per environment and renders its own rows. The comment also records why `aggregateIdFor` cannot answer this, so the next reader does not move the line back.

SCOPE HELD (rail 5): nothing under `apps/daemon/src/deployment` changed — `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/deployment` is EMPTY. This row decides what is OFFERED; the engine, its refusal order and its receipt stay other rows'.

VERIFIED SO FAR: `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/daemon/tsconfig.json` clean, and the four affordance test files pass — `Test Files 4 passed (4)` / `Tests 112 passed (112)`, 8.57s, EXIT 0. No existing arm broke. The new arms that prove the id by value are step 4's.

NOTE: `deployment.set_target` deliberately keeps the project fallthrough. Only `deployment.deploy` is goal-scoped, because only it is what the card matches; giving set_target a goal key would invent an identity no consumer asked for.

WITHHOLDING LANDED (DoD 2) AND THE GRANULARITY DECISION IS WRITTEN DOWN (DoD 3). One design change from the step's literal wording, for a reason an existing test forced.

WITHHOLDING IS EXPRESSED AS A MISSING PREREQUISITE, NOT AS A SKIPPED PUSH. The step says "emit the deployment offer only when a target IS bound". A bare `if (bound) offers.push(...)` would have reddened an existing arm that is truer than anything I would have written: affordance-read.test.ts:563 asserts SET EQUALITY between emitted offers and READY steps — `expect(offered).toEqual(expected)` — so a step left READY with its offer skipped breaks the invariant "every READY step carries an offer, and no offer exists for a kind no step called READY". I routed the fact through `surfaceMissing` instead (:229-246), which already appends a SYNTHETIC missing prerequisite for `project.activate`. Unbound target therefore yields `missing: [..., "deployment.set_target"]`, the step returns BLOCKED before any offer is pushed, and BOTH sides of the invariant move together. Absent AND named beats absent and silent: the operator's card is gone (rail 2, not a dead button) and the surface says which command would restore it.

I DID NOT PUT IT IN `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES`, and the table says why in its own words. bootstrap-sequence.ts:47-55 deliberately excludes `deployment.set_target` from `deployment.deploy`'s row: that table reads COMMITTED KINDS, so naming it there "would admit a deploy of `production` on the strength of a target bound for `staging` — coarser than the rule it claims to enforce". My check reads the actual per-environment durable binding, which is the finer-grained read that comment says belongs elsewhere. I quoted that reasoning at the new site so the next reader does not tidy it into the table.

BOUND IS READ THROUGH THE LANDED READER, NOT RE-DERIVED. `productionDeployPorts(config.store, config.projectId).target` (deploy-command.ts:89, task-79f8c7c0) — it resolves `deploy-target:<projectId>:<environment>`, decodes with the setter's own decoder, and fails closed to null on an unreadable or invalid binding. Composed ONCE per port, not once per read. `AffordancePortConfig` gains an OPTIONAL `deployTarget?: DeployTargetPort` purely as a test seam; production never passes it. No import cycle: `deployment/deploy-command.ts` imports `http/http-async-contract.js` and `http/http-contract.js`, never `http/affordance-read.js`.

"BOUND" NEEDS A ROSTER, AND THE ANSWER TO STEP 7's QUESTION FALLS OUT OF IT. `DeployTargetPort` takes an environment, so I ask the closed roster `ENVIRONMENT_NAMES = ["preview", "production", "verify"]` (environment-contracts.ts:29) and bound means SOME environment has a target. Consequence, stated at the site and answering step 7's self-review question directly: a goal with `preview` bound and `production` unbound IS OFFERED. That is correct rather than lax — the offer is one per goal with the environment chosen at dispatch, so it can only mean "deploying this goal is possible"; the per-environment refusal stays with the engine (`DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING`, before any docker spawn) and the card already renders "No target is bound for this environment yet." per row.

DoD 3's COMMENT is at the offer-identity site (bootstrapAggregateId) and carries the reasoning, not a restatement: one offer per goal; environment chosen at dispatch and carried in the payload (`["environment", "sha"]`), so a per-environment offer would put the environment in two places that can disagree; the durable target keyed per (project, environment) is a DIFFERENT axis deliberately absent from the offer identity; the card reads it and renders its own rows.

VERIFIED: `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/daemon/tsconfig.json` clean. All four affordance test files pass unchanged — `Test Files 4 passed (4)` / `Tests 112 passed (112)`, EXIT 0. They stay green because both sides of the set-equality moved together, which is the invariant working, not the arm missing the change; the arms that prove the new behaviour by value are step 4's.

RAIL 5 HELD: `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/deployment` is EMPTY.

DISCLOSED, NOT MINE TO FIX: `affordance-read.ts` is 566 lines and was ALREADY 522 at HEAD — over the rail's 400 split threshold before this row touched it. implementationPlan.description:
THE PRODUCTION-SURFACE ARMS (DoD 1, 2, 3) - in `apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.test.ts`.

ASSERT AGAINST THE PRODUCTION SURFACE READ, not a hand-built frame (DoD 1). A frame you construct proves the matcher string, not that the surface emits it.

(a) A goal whose project HAS a bound target: the offered set contains `deployment.deploy` with `targetAggregateId` EQUAL BY VALUE to `deploy:<goalId>`. Compare against the exact string the card uses; do not regex it.
(b) WITHHELD: a goal whose project has NO bound target. ASSERT THE OFFERED-KIND SET (DoD 2 says so explicitly) so that "offers nothing for deploy" and "offers something else instead" are ONE assertion - a `not.toContain` alone passes if the surface emitted a differently-named deployment offer.
(c) THE DECIDED SHAPE (DoD 3): assert exactly one deploy offer per goal, not one per environment, with two environments bound. That is the arm that pins the granularity decision so a later change cannot quietly switch axes.
(d) DoD 4: assert the card's EXACT matcher finds the goal-scoped offer and does NOT find a stale project-scoped one. Reproduce the matcher literally in the test. Then NAME IN THE COMPLETION RECORD whether the generic path at :282-284 still emits a project-targeted deployment offer as well and, if so, why it is harmless - if both exist, the card must still match exactly one.
implementationPlan.note:
FOUR ARMS ADDED, ALL AGAINST THE PRODUCTION SURFACE READ. `Test Files 4 passed (4)` / `Tests 116 passed (116)` across all four affordance files, EXIT 0 — 112 before, so the four are new and every pre-existing arm still passes.

(a) DoD 1 — "targets the goal by value, so the card's exact matcher finds it". Bound target, then `targetAggregateId` is compared with `toBe(`deploy:${goalId}`)`, never a regex, and separately asserted `not.toBe(BOOTSTRAP_PROJECT)`.
(b) DoD 2 — "withholds the offer entirely when no environment has a bound target". Asserts the SET, as DoD 2 demands: `offers.map(kind).filter(startsWith("deployment."))` equals exactly `["deployment.set_target"]`. A `not.toContain` would have passed on a differently-named deployment offer; this also pins that withholding the deploy does NOT withhold the sibling that fixes it. Plus the card matcher returns `[]`, and the step is `{ status: "BLOCKED", missing: ["deployment.set_target"] }` — absent AND named.
(c) DoD 3 — "emits ONE offer per goal with two environments bound, not one per environment". Two environments bound, exactly one offer. This is the arm that pins the granularity axis so a later change cannot switch it quietly.
(d) DoD 4 — the card's matcher is reproduced LITERALLY as `cardMatches` (`commandKind === "deployment.deploy" && targetAggregateId === `deploy:${goalId}``), asserted to find exactly ONE, and a companion assertion proves no PROJECT-targeted `deployment.deploy` offer survives beside it.
A fifth arm pins the one-of-two-environments answer: `preview` bound and `production` not IS offered, because the offer means "deploying this goal is possible" and the per-environment refusal is the engine's.

THE GOAL ID IS DERIVED FROM THE SURFACE, NOT RESTATED. `goalOf` reads `read.planningGoalRefs` — the SAME resolution `soleLegacyPlanningSubject` consumes to build the subject — and pins it to the fixture's goal by value. My first attempt read it off the `goal.close` step's `aggregateId` and failed with `expected null to be 'goal-1'`: a BLOCKED step carries `aggregateId: null`. Deriving it from a deployment step would have made the DoD-1 arm circular, so `planningGoalRefs` is the right source.

A SECOND FAILURE WORTH RECORDING, because it is a real prerequisite fact. With the world driven only to `approval.decide` every arm failed with `expected [] to have a length of 1` — no deploy offer at ANY binding. Cause: `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES["deployment.deploy"] = ["repository.publish"]` (a deploy builds THE LANDED SHA), so the step is BLOCKED on the publish and no target binding can make it offer. The fixture sequence is project.register, bind_repository, provider.probe, policy.install x2, policy.validate, project.activate, goal.create, plan.propose x2, approval.decide, repository.publish, goal.close — so the world must be driven to `goal.close` to run PAST the publish. Both diagnoses are quoted in the test's own comments so the next reader does not re-derive them.

DoD 4's COMPLETION-RECORD QUESTION, answered precisely and with its limit stated. Does the generic path at :282-284 still emit a PROJECT-targeted deployment offer? For `deployment.deploy`: only when `planningSubject` is NULL. `bootstrapAggregateId` resolves the goal-scoped key inside `if (planningSubject !== null)`; with a null subject it falls through to `aggregateIdFor`, whose `default` returns `subject ?? projectId`, and `DEFAULT_SUBJECTS` has no deployment entry — so the id is the project. `soleLegacyPlanningSubject` returns null when `planningGoalRefs` does not hold exactly one entry with a legacy offer, i.e. on a surface with zero or several planning goals. HARMLESS: the Deployments card only renders inside an OPENED goal and matches `deploy:${goalId}` exactly, so a project-targeted row can never match it; and on a surface with no sole planning goal there is no goal card to render into. Note also that the withholding rule applies in BOTH branches — with no bound target there is no deploy offer at all, project-targeted or otherwise. THIS PARAGRAPH IS REASONED FROM SOURCE, NOT MEASURED BY AN ARM: isolating a subject-null world that has nonetheless committed `repository.publish` needs a second planning goal, which is fixture work beyond this row. I am labelling it rather than implying I ran it. `deployment.set_target` keeps the project fallthrough unconditionally and is not matched by the card at all.

PEER DIRT UNTOUCHED: my block is appended at the END of the file; task-9aea412b's hunks around :473-545 are intact (`UNCARDED_SERVED_KINDS ... Object.freeze([])` still at :484). Nothing reverted, stashed or restaged. `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/daemon/tsconfig.json` clean.

implementationPlan.note:
WHOLE-TREE CENSUS DONE. RESULT: NO CONSUMER NEEDED AN ARM, and every verdict below is measured, not assumed.
